The short version

A distinctive cherry-wood experiment with attractive bitter-fruit development and strong disagreement about wood and floral character. The actual label controls the strength.

Exact identity: Lot No. 40 Rye Explorations Release No. 03 Cherry Wood Casks, photographed April 2024 bottling, NAS, 53.5% ABV / 107 proof, 750 mL.

Background and history

The producer shop was published October 8, 2024 and the photographed bottle states April 2024. The autumn 2024 independent review documents the original release era.

Bottle number 1800 in the producer photograph is an individual number, not a verified total production count. Older and newer review sessions show substantial disagreement.

For the shared historical context, read Canadian whisky, cross-border trade and the American market. The release chronology above distinguishes the current bottle from its brand’s earlier history.

Producer, grains, aging and finishing

Producer specifies new white-oak aging then European cherry-wood casks. Its own photograph visibly states April 2024 and 53.5%; this agrees with Dramface and Québec Whisky. Current product prose rounds or misstates strength as 54%, so the verified 53.5% pack controls this dossier. No separate 54% edition is invented. Finish duration and complete component ages remain unknown.

Critical review synthesis

Aengus McCloud · Dramface

Initially compelling bitter orange/cherry and oily development become less vivid over weeks as wood grows stronger. Musty and cleaner-like aromas remain explicit reservations.

Scope: November 18, 2024 exact 53.5% bottle; long-term aging hopes are not proven future results.

André, Patrick and Kim · Québec Whisky

André and Patrick enjoy textured fruit/spice and a developed ending. Kim instead finds unpleasant floral/earthy dominance and wonders about sample variation.

Scope: July 2025 / February 2026 exact 53.5% reviews, translated French; one platform with genuine disagreement, not a unanimous panel.

Published sample evidence, not first-person tasting or a representative survey. Reviewer disagreement and recipe-era limitations remain explicit; publisher grades are not mechanically converted.

Quality and calibration

Quality 6.3 / 10. Good but contentious provisional Canadian all-rye execution. Fruit/bitter-herbal development and body receive support; growing wood dominance, rough aromas and markedly unfavorable floral impressions constrain integration and finish. Novel wood and rarity add no points.

No defensible complete Canadian native 1/5/10 framework is established for this comparison group. Seven universal execution dimensions are assessed within Canadian Single Grain / 100% Rye; unrelated American bourbon and straight-rye endpoints are not imported.

Serving recommendations

Neat

Try a small full-strength pour and allow time in the glass; the matched accounts disagree on some finish and cask effects.

Water / rocks

Add only a few drops at a time and compare texture. Several reviewers find too much dilution reduces definition.

Old Fashioned

Keep syrup restrained; a recurring core rye is the price comparison before mixing a limited bottle.

Manhattan / highball

Try a small serve with vermouth or soda, adjusting sweetness and dilution to the cask influence.

Serving suggestions are editorial starting points, grounded in documented strength and style; adjust to your taste.
